title: runtime-multiplexer-model-prognosticator-routing-acceptance-metrics-and-safety-fallback
creator: Lena Novak
description:
Objective: Design and prototype a lightweight runtime multiplexer ("multiplexer") that uses a compact "model prognosticator" to predict whether
a fast, small-footprint model variant will produce an acceptable continuation. The goal is
to capture most of the latency/cost wins from optimistic routing while providing strict
telemetry and a deterministic, low-latency fallback path when confidence is low.

Background: Existing speculative-decode approaches at Redwood use prefill probes and
confidence signals tightly coupled to heavy-weight probes; operational complexity and
kernel-affinity mismatches have led to corner-case tail latency regressions. This ticket
explores an orthogonal design: a small prognostic model that runs at the request ingress
(CPU or small GPU) to score route candidates and select the best-serving variant with a
multiplexer that is kernel-aware (schedules requests to backends whose kernels match the
predicted decode profile).

Proposed Design:
- Model Prognosticator: a 1-2 layer lightweight transformer/logistic ensemble trained on
  historical (prefix, latent) features to predict the acceptance probability of fast
  variants for the next N tokens. Runs as a fast inline scorer with <1ms p50 on CPU for
  typical prefix sizes.
- Routing Multiplexer: receives prognosticator scores + kernel-capability fingerprint and
  chooses one of three lanes: FAST (low-cost quantized variant), BALANCED (medium),
  CONSERVATIVE (high-quality, standard) with soft timeboxes. The multiplexer also annotates
  selection with reason codes for observability.
- Kernel-aware Scheduling: multiplexer consults a small kernel index that maps model
  variants + sequence-length buckets to preferred GPU kernels (fused attention, flash,
  quantized matmuls). Scheduling hints are included in the request metadata to avoid
  runtime kernel-mismatch penalties.
- Lightweight Prefill Strategy: when FAST lane is chosen, we run a brief inline prefix
  analyzer to capture attention-window density and key-value size; this allows the runtime
  to pre-allocate or short-circuit KV cache ops for the fast path.

Acceptance Metrics (what we will measure):
- Acceptance AUC (prognosticator): area under ROC for predicting that FAST outputs match
  CONSERVATIVE outputs on a token-level equivalence metric.
- False Accept Rate (FAR): proportion of FAST-accepted decisions where downstream quality
  falls below the degrade threshold. Target FAR < 1%.
- Tail-latency delta: 95/99p latency reduction for FAST vs CONSERVATIVE lane. Target p99
  improvement >= 25% without increasing p999.
- Cost per token delta: end-to-end token compute cost reduction when using multiplexer vs
  always-serving CONSERVATIVE.
- Rollback incidence: number of automatic fallbacks triggered per 10k requests; target < 5.

Fallback and Safety Plan:
- Deterministic Timebox: when FAST lane decoding stalls or produces low-confidence tokens,
  the multiplexer enforces a tight timebox (e.g., 50ms) and then forwards the request to
  CONSERVATIVE lane (soft handoff).
- Circuit Breaker: a rolling-window circuit that disables FAST lane for a model variant if FAR
  exceeds threshold or if p99 CPU/GPU tail increases beyond SLO. Automated alerts publish
  incident context to oncall and create a tracking Linear issue.
- Staged Rollouts: enable multiplexer behind a feature flag with percent-based traffic
  ramp (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%) and automatic metrics gates at each step.

Telemetry & Dashboards:
- Per-lane counters (requests, accepts, fallbacks) and reason-code histograms.
- Prognosticator calibration dashboard (score distribution vs empirical acceptance).
- Kernel-affinity mismatch heatmap (requests annotated where selected kernel != runtime kernel).
- Rollforward/rollback events log with correlating trace IDs for replay.

Milestones:
1) Prototype prognosticator + synthetic workload (ETA: 2 wks)
2) Integrate multiplexer in staging runtime, kernel-index sync (ETA: +2 wks)
3) Canary rollout at 0.1% with gating metrics and dashboards (ETA: +1 wk)
4) Expand traffic and tune thresholds; prepare runbook for oncall (ETA: +2 wks)

Success Criteria: p99 latency reduction for targeted workloads, FAR < 1%, stable rollout with
circuit-breaker preventing customer-visible regressions.

Non-goals: this ticket does not include full model re-training pipelines for the prognosticator
(that will be tracked separately) and does not change billing primitives.
routing_strategy: kernel-aware multiplexer with FAST/BALANCED/CONSERVATIVE lanes; prognosticator scores + kernel index drive selection; timeboxed handoffs for safety.
fallback_plan: Deterministic timebox -> soft handoff to CONSERVATIVE; rolling-window circuit breaker disables FAST lane on thresholds; staged percent rollout with metric gates and automated rollback.
